title: Pain Score Trend Post-Analgesia
scenario: A 62-year-old male client reports severe incisional pain after abdominal surgery. The nurse administers IV opioid analgesia and reassesses pain and sedation over the next hour.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: Considering the full trend, what is the nurse's priority concern at 10:00?

options.text: Increasing sedation with a declining respiratory rate and SpO2
Inadequate pain relief from the opioid
The client is at risk for an allergic reaction
The pain score is dropping too slowly

questions.rationale: Although pain is well controlled, the deepening sedation (RASS -2), falling respiratory rate to 14, and dropping SpO2 indicate opioid-induced respiratory depression, which is the priority concern.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: Based on the trend at 10:00, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stimulate the client and encourage deep breathing
Withhold the next opioid dose and notify the provider
Continue to monitor respiratory rate and SpO2 closely
Administer an additional opioid dose for comfort
Apply restraints to keep the client still

questions.rationale: With rising sedation and respiratory depression, the nurse stimulates the client, holds further opioids, monitors closely, and keeps naloxone ready. Giving more opioid would worsen the depression; restraints are not indicated.
